solution:
For \({}^{14}_{7}\text{N}\) the nucleus holds \(Z = 7\) protons and \(N = A - Z = 14 - 7 = 7\) neutrons.

The binding energy is the energy equivalent of the mass defect. Working with the atomic mass of hydrogen \(m_H = 1.007825\,\text{u}\) rather than the bare proton mass lets the 7 orbital electrons on the left cancel the 7 carried by the atomic mass \(m({}^{14}_{7}\text{N})\) on the right, so

\(\Delta m = Z\,m_H + N\,m_n - m\!\left({}^{14}_{7}\text{N}\right)\)

\(\Delta m = 7(1.007825\,\text{u}) + 7(1.008665\,\text{u}) - 14.00307\,\text{u}\)

\(\Delta m = 7.054775\,\text{u} + 7.060655\,\text{u} - 14.00307\,\text{u} = 0.11236\,\text{u}\)

Using \(1\,\text{u} \equiv 931.5\,\text{MeV}/c^2\),

\(E_b = \Delta m\,c^2 = 0.11236 \times 931.5\,\text{MeV} = 104.66\,\text{MeV}\)

(The binding energy per nucleon is \(104.66/14 = 7.48\,\text{MeV}\), consistent with a light nucleus lying below the \(8.8\,\text{MeV}\) peak of the curve.)

Binding energy of \({}^{14}_{7}\text{N} \approx 104.7\,\text{MeV}\)

In each case \(\Delta m = Z\,m_H + (A - Z)\,m_n - m(\text{atom})\), with atomic masses used throughout so that the \(Z\) electron masses cancel between the two sides, and \(E_b = \Delta m \times 931.5\,\text{MeV}\).

For \({}^{56}_{26}\text{Fe}\): \(Z = 26\), \(N = 56 - 26 = 30\).

\(\Delta m = 26(1.007825\,\text{u}) + 30(1.008665\,\text{u}) - 55.934939\,\text{u}\)

\(\Delta m = 26.203450\,\text{u} + 30.259950\,\text{u} - 55.934939\,\text{u} = 0.528461\,\text{u}\)

\(E_b = 0.528461 \times 931.5\,\text{MeV} = 492.26\,\text{MeV}\), i.e. \(492.26/56 = 8.79\,\text{MeV}\) per nucleon.

For \({}^{209}_{83}\text{Bi}\): \(Z = 83\), \(N = 209 - 83 = 126\).

\(\Delta m = 83(1.007825\,\text{u}) + 126(1.008665\,\text{u}) - 208.980388\,\text{u}\)

\(\Delta m = 83.649475\,\text{u} + 127.091790\,\text{u} - 208.980388\,\text{u} = 1.760877\,\text{u}\)

\(E_b = 1.760877 \times 931.5\,\text{MeV} = 1640.26\,\text{MeV}\), i.e. \(1640.26/209 = 7.85\,\text{MeV}\) per nucleon.

The heavier nucleus has the larger total binding energy but the smaller binding energy per nucleon, which is why \({}^{209}_{83}\text{Bi}\) is the less tightly bound of the two.

(a) \(E_b\!\left({}^{56}_{26}\text{Fe}\right) \approx 492.26\,\text{MeV}\)

(b) \(E_b\!\left({}^{209}_{83}\text{Bi}\right) \approx 1640.26\,\text{MeV}\)

Separating every nucleon of every nucleus in the coin costs exactly the total binding energy of all the nuclei present.

Number of atoms in \(3.0\,\text{g}\) of \({}^{63}_{29}\text{Cu}\), whose gram atomic mass is \(62.92960\,\text{g}\):

\(N = \dfrac{3.0}{62.92960} \times 6.023 \times 10^{23} = 2.871 \times 10^{22}\) atoms

Binding energy of one \({}^{63}_{29}\text{Cu}\) nucleus, with \(Z = 29\) and \(N = 63 - 29 = 34\):

\(\Delta m = 29(1.007825\,\text{u}) + 34(1.008665\,\text{u}) - 62.92960\,\text{u}\)

\(\Delta m = 29.226925\,\text{u} + 34.294610\,\text{u} - 62.92960\,\text{u} = 0.591935\,\text{u}\)

\(E_b = 0.591935 \times 931.5\,\text{MeV} = 551.39\,\text{MeV}\) per nucleus

Total energy required:

\(E = N E_b = \left(2.871 \times 10^{22}\right)\left(551.39\,\text{MeV}\right) = 1.58 \times 10^{25}\,\text{MeV}\)

In SI units, using \(1\,\text{MeV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-13}\,\text{J}\),

\(E = 1.58 \times 10^{25} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-13}\,\text{J} = 2.5 \times 10^{12}\,\text{J}\)

This is an enormous energy for a 3 g coin, which is precisely why nucleons are never separated in ordinary chemical or mechanical processes.

Energy required \(\approx 1.58 \times 10^{25}\,\text{MeV} = 2.5 \times 10^{12}\,\text{J}\)

For \({}^{1}_{1}\text{H} + {}^{3}_{1}\text{H} \to {}^{2}_{1}\text{H} + {}^{2}_{1}\text{H}\), the total electron count is the same on both sides (\(1 + 1 = 1 + 1\)), so the electron masses cancel and the atomic masses supplied may be substituted directly into the \(Q\) formula.

\(Q = \left[\,m\!\left({}^{1}_{1}\text{H}\right) + m\!\left({}^{3}_{1}\text{H}\right) - 2\,m\!\left({}^{2}_{1}\text{H}\right)\right]c^2\)

Taking \(m\!\left({}^{1}_{1}\text{H}\right) = m_H = 1.007825\,\text{u}\),

\(Q = \left[1.007825 + 3.016049 - 2(2.014102)\right]\text{u} \times c^2\)

\(Q = \left[4.023874 - 4.028204\right]\text{u} \times c^2 = -0.004330\,\text{u} \times c^2\)

\(Q = -0.004330 \times 931.5\,\text{MeV} = -4.03\,\text{MeV}\)

The products are heavier than the reactants, so mass increases and energy must be supplied for the reaction to proceed; a negative \(Q\) means the reaction absorbs energy.

\(Q = -4.03\,\text{MeV}\); the reaction is endothermic.
_note: The stem says the masses 'refer to the respective nuclei' but the data supplied are ATOMIC masses (the deuteron nucleus is 2.013553 u, not the printed 2.014102 u). This is NCERT's own standing wording; it does not change the answer here because the electron count balances (1+1 on each side), so I have used the atomic masses as printed and said so in the solution. m(1H) is not in the stem's own data list — it is taken as m_H = 1.007825 u from the shared constants table that opens the EXERCISES block.

solution:
For \({}^{12}_{6}\text{C} + {}^{12}_{6}\text{C} \to {}^{20}_{10}\text{Ne} + {}^{4}_{2}\text{He}\), the electron count balances (\(6 + 6 = 10 + 2\)), so the atomic masses supplied may be substituted directly into the \(Q\) formula.

\(Q = \left[\,2\,m\!\left({}^{12}_{6}\text{C}\right) - m\!\left({}^{20}_{10}\text{Ne}\right) - m\!\left({}^{4}_{2}\text{He}\right)\right]c^2\)

Taking \(m\!\left({}^{4}_{2}\text{He}\right) = 4.002603\,\text{u}\),

\(Q = \left[2(12.000000) - 19.992439 - 4.002603\right]\text{u} \times c^2\)

\(Q = \left[24.000000 - 23.995042\right]\text{u} \times c^2 = 0.004958\,\text{u} \times c^2\)

\(Q = 0.004958 \times 931.5\,\text{MeV} = 4.62\,\text{MeV}\)

The products are lighter than the reactants, so the lost mass appears as kinetic energy of the products; a positive \(Q\) means the reaction releases energy.

\(Q = +4.62\,\text{MeV}\); the reaction is exothermic.
_note: m(4He) is not in the stem's own data list — it is taken as 4.002603 u from the shared constants table that opens the EXERCISES block. Same nuclei-vs-atomic-mass wording point as Ex 13.5(i): the electron count balances (6+6 = 10+2), so the printed atomic masses give the correct Q unchanged.
